description:
Snehasparsham is a welfare scheme initiated by the Government of India aimed at providing support to children in difficult circumstances. 

The scheme was launched on 1st April 2021. 

It was introduced under the Ministry of Women and Child Development. 

The primary objective of Snehasparsham is to ensure that children who are orphaned or abandoned receive the necessary care and support. 

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to these children to meet their basic needs. 

The target beneficiaries of the scheme include children aged 0 to 18 years. 

These children must be orphans or abandoned and without any parental support. 

The financial assistance provided under the scheme is set at ₹2,000 per month for each eligible child. 

This amount is intended to cover essential expenses such as food, clothing, and education. 

The scheme also aims to facilitate the rehabilitation of these children into society. 

It encourages the establishment of Child Care Institutions to provide a safe environment for these children. 

The scheme has a specific goal of reaching at least 10,000 children in its first year of implementation. 

The timeline for achieving this target is set for the end of the fiscal year 2021-2022. 

To be eligible for the benefits of Snehasparsham, children must be registered with the Child Welfare Committee. 

The application process requires the submission of specific documents. 

These documents include proof of age, proof of abandonment or orphan status, and identity proof. 

The application must be submitted to the local Child Welfare Committee. 

Once the application is received, the committee conducts a verification process. 

This verification includes home visits and interviews to assess the child's situation. 

Following successful verification, the financial assistance is disbursed monthly. 

The disbursement is made directly to the bank account of the Child Care Institution or the guardian. 

The scheme is implemented through various state governments and local bodies. 

Each state has its own Child Welfare Committee responsible for overseeing the implementation. 

The Ministry of Women and Child Development provides guidelines and support to these committees. 

The scheme also includes provisions for educational support. 

Children under this scheme are encouraged to enroll in schools and receive formal education. 

The government collaborates with NGOs to provide additional support services. 

This includes counseling and vocational training for older children. 

The aim is to ensure that children are not only supported financially but also equipped with skills for future employment. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to improve child welfare in India. 

It aligns with the National Policy for Children 2013, which emphasizes the rights of children. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹100 crores for the implementation of Snehasparsham in its initial phase. 

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted regularly to assess its impact. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme continuously. 

The scheme also aims to raise awareness about child rights and welfare among the general public. 

Workshops and seminars are organized to educate communities about the importance of supporting vulnerable children. 

The government encourages public participation in the welfare of these children. 

Individuals and organizations are invited to contribute through donations and volunteer work. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders. 

Many NGOs have expressed support for the initiative and are willing to collaborate. 

The success of Snehasparsham is measured through the number of children rehabilitated and supported. 

Regular reports are published to provide transparency and accountability. 

The scheme has the potential to significantly improve the lives of thousands of children across India. 

It addresses a critical gap in the support system for orphans and abandoned children. 

The government is committed to expanding the reach of the scheme in the coming years. 

Plans are underway to enhance the financial assistance amount based on inflation and cost of living. 

The scheme also aims to integrate technology for better tracking and monitoring of beneficiaries. 

Digital platforms are being developed to streamline the application and disbursement processes. 

The long-term vision of Snehasparsham is to create a society where every child has access to basic needs and opportunities for growth. 

By focusing on both immediate assistance and long-term rehabilitation, the scheme seeks to break the cycle of poverty and neglect. 

The government is actively seeking partnerships with educational institutions to facilitate learning opportunities for children under the scheme. 

This holistic approach ensures that children not only survive but thrive in a supportive environment. 

The implementation of Snehasparsham reflects the government's commitment to child welfare and protection. 

It is a crucial step towards ensuring that no child is left behind in the pursuit of a better future. 

The scheme is expected to evolve based on the changing needs of children and society. 

Regular assessments will guide the government in making necessary adjustments to the program. 

Overall, Snehasparsham represents a significant effort to uplift and empower vulnerable children in India. 

The initiative is a testament to the belief that every child deserves a chance to succeed. 

Through targeted support and community involvement, the scheme aims to foster a nurturing environment for all children. 

The government encourages all citizens to play a role in supporting this noble cause. 

By working together, it is possible to create a brighter future for the children of India.
